_comment: Time-boxed npm audit exceptions for the Worker's dependency tree.
Enforced by scripts/hooks/check_npm_audit.py, NOT by npm — npm audit has
no native ignore mechanism, so a bare `npm audit` is all-or-nothing.
Every entry MUST carry: the advisory id, why it is accepted, the ticket
that removes it, and an ISO expiry. An expired entry fails the build, so
an exception cannot outlive its argument.
This does NOT reintroduce the --omit=dev shortcut this job rejected
earlier. That was rejected because `npm audit fix` cleared everything with
package.json unchanged — a fix existed and was being skipped. Here no fix
exists at any version, which is a different situation and is why each
entry has to say so explicitly.

allow.reason: libheif vulnerabilities reached via sharp <- miniflare <- wrangler / @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers. sharp is NOT a declared dependency of this Worker; it arrives transitively with miniflare, the local Workers simulator. It runs on a developer machine and in CI, never in the deployed Worker - Cloudflare Workers cannot execute native binaries at all, so this code path does not exist in production. Verified 2026-09-09: no forward fix exists. @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers is already at latest (0.22.0), and every wrangler >= 4.16.0 depends on a vulnerable miniflare. npm's only offered fix is `--force`, which downgrades vitest-pool-workers 0.22.0 -> 0.8.30, a breaking change to the test runner. Trading a dev-only advisory for a broken test suite is the worse deal.
